tierWindow.goal: Build a toolkit of specific active techniques matched to how you learn, match technique to the exam type ahead of you, and perform a monitored, optimised exam-day strategy.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Evaluation and design (evaluate, select, design, adapt), beyond the intermediate tier's apply/select-family level, toward independent judgement and transfer under real exam conditions.
tierWindow.taskComplexity: Open, self-directed tasks: assembling a personal toolkit across three technique families, judging which technique suits which exam format, and running a monitored real-time performance.
tierWindow.autonomy: Low scaffolding. The learner adapts and designs their own combination of techniques and exam-day practice; worked examples show self-directed adaptation rather than a fixed sequence to follow.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: The learner already has a revision strategy built around their use of time and the gaps in their knowledge, and already knows that active techniques outperform passive review, including how to select a technique family to fit their material (the intermediate tier). They have not yet built a full toolkit of specific techniques within each family, matched their technique choice to the type of exam they will sit, or planned and monitored their own performance in the exam room itself.

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has four short lessons. First, the active-technique toolkit itself: the specific techniques within the visual, auditory and kinaesthetic families. Second, matching your choice of technique to the type of exam you are preparing for, not only to the material. Third, performing on exam day itself, from arrival to writing to time. Fourth, bringing the toolkit, the exam-type match and exam-day execution together into one monitored performance. Work through them in order; the last lesson depends on the first three.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the four lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This course assumes you already have a revision strategy built around your use of time and the gaps in your knowledge, and already know that active techniques outperform passive review. It takes that further: by the end you will be able to select and apply specific techniques from across the visual, auditory and kinaesthetic families, match your choice of technique to the format of the exam ahead of you, and plan and monitor your own performance on exam day itself.

None of this assumes a fixed sequence to follow. It assumes you are ready to design your own combination of techniques and run your own exam-day performance, and shows you what that combination needs to account for.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: select and apply specific active techniques across technique families, match technique to exam type, plan and monitor exam-day performance.

practiceConnection.academic: Matching a method to the demands of a specific task, rather than defaulting to whatever worked last time, is a judgement call you will keep making well beyond exam revision. The same discipline, checking what a task actually requires before choosing how to approach it, applies directly to coursework design and professional practice.

decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Revision is no longer a technique family chosen once and applied regardless: you can select and apply specific techniques from across the visual, auditory and kinaesthetic families, match your choice of technique to the format of the exam you are facing, and plan and monitor your own performance on exam day itself, from arrival through to writing to time. Look back at the confidence check: comparing where you started with where you are now shows how far this has moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, treating a technique choice as a judgement matched to the task in front of you, rather than a habit applied regardless, is one you can carry into any sustained piece of academic or professional preparation where the format of the final test matters as much as the material.
